title: Callsite Snapshotter: Replayable, Low‑Overhead Trace Snapshots for Debugging
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Debugging production trace anomalies is time-consuming because traces are incomplete, sampling differs across services, and reproducing a request with the same request-context (prefix, sampling decision, provenance) is hard. Goal: Implement a lightweight 'Callsite Snapshotter' tracing hook in server SDKs that captures a minimal, deterministic snapshot of request provenance and event anchors (callsite ids, sampling hint, KV fingerprints) that can be attached to logs, surface in Console, and used to replay or reason about traces without needing full-span capture. The snapshotter must add <1% CPU and <500B payload per request on p95 traffic profiles, be compatible with existing header carriers (HTTP/gRPC/websocket), and integrate with sampling budget enforcement and Console debugging flows.
acceptance_criteria: SDK hook implemented in Node and Go: automatic snapshot emission for sampled and non-sampled requests
Snapshot serialized to existing request-envelopes header and mapped to a compact log field in logs and telemetry
Console displays snapshot context alongside trace links and exposes a 'replayable snapshot' download (JSON) for SREs
End-to-end test demonstrating that replayed snapshot can rehydrate sampling hint and callsite anchors in a local dev environment
Overhead benchmark: <1% CPU at p95 and median extra payload <500 bytes for typical request sizes
Security review completed for provenance headers and replay artifact download
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff with Observability and SDK teams. Drafted protobuf for minimal snapshot fields: provenance_id, callsite_ids[], sampling_hint, kv_fingerprint, timestamp_ms.
2026-02-21: Node SDK prototype emits snapshot as X-RW-SNAPSHOT header (base64 compact JSON). Microbenchmarks show ~350B avg payload and ~0.6% CPU overhead on local p95 workload.
2026-02-27: Go SDK implementation completed. Added carrier normalization for http/gRPC. Integration tests passing in staging.
2026-03-03: UX session with Console team to define snapshot display and 'download snapshot' permission model. Agreed snapshots will be visible to admins and SRE roles by default.
2026-03-06: Security review kickoff. Draft threat model added to Confluence. Flagged need to scrub personally-identifiable payloads from snapshot serialization.
2026-03-08: End-to-end replay harness PR opened (github #8342). Need to add deterministic seed for KV fingerprinting to make replay stable across runs.
comments: Priya Desai (PM) 2026-02-18: This solves a real SRE pain point—please ensure snapshots are opt-out per service and don't change existing sampling semantics.
Jordan Weiss (SRE) 2026-02-24: Prototype looks promising. Suggest adding a TTL on snapshot artifacts in Console to avoid long-term storage of transient provenance.
Security Review (sec-team) 2026-03-06: Ensure replay artifacts are scanned for secrets before download. Recommend adding redaction hooks in SDK serializer.
Liam Chen (Eng) 2026-03-07: We'll add a serializer plugin point so teams can register redaction rules; default will drop headers listed in global secret-config.
Design Review (Console) 2026-03-05: Display should include a compact 'provenance fingerprint' and a link to reconstructed trace when available. Keep UI read-only for snapshot JSON.
next_steps: Add deterministic KV fingerprint seed and write integration test to validate replay equivalence
Implement redaction plugin and run security scan on preview snapshots
Wire Console download button and retention policy (7 days default)
Add A/B rollout flag to enable snapshot emission per service/team for first week
